question: How many new cars were registered in the UK in September 2026?

target.what: New passenger car registrations in the United Kingdom, as reported by the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders (SMMT). This counts new cars registered for the first time, including private, fleet, and business registrations, but excludes used cars and light commercial vehicles.
target.publisher: Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders (SMMT)
target.caveats: The target period is completed relative to the information cutoff of 2026-10-15. SMMT typically publishes September registration data in early October, so the figure may already be available. If not, estimates must rely on historical seasonality, related series, or forecasts. The target value can be estimated by applying the typical September share of annual registrations to a forecast or partial-year total, or by using the most recent September value adjusted for trend.

candidates.hypothesis: DVLA new vehicle registrations data may provide a close proxy for SMMT figures, though definitions and timing may differ slightly. The ratio between DVLA and SMMT figures can be used to bridge if SMMT data is unavailable.
candidates.data_to_find: DVLA new car registrations for September 2026 or recent months, and historical comparison between DVLA and SMMT monthly figures to establish a conversion factor.

candidates.hypothesis: UK car production and import volumes in the months leading up to September can indicate supply available for registration. However, registrations are demand-driven and may not equal production plus imports minus exports due to inventory changes.
candidates.data_to_find: UK car production figures for July and August 2026 from SMMT, and import/export data for cars from HMRC or trade bodies. Also inventory levels if available.

candidates.hypothesis: The September share of annual registrations is relatively stable, typically around 15-20%. Using a reliable estimate of the 2026 annual total (from forecasts or year-to-date extrapolation) and the historical September share can yield an estimate.
candidates.data_to_find: Historical September share of annual UK new car registrations for the last 5-10 years, and a forecast or estimate for total 2026 registrations.

candidates.hypothesis: Factors such as interest rates, consumer confidence, electric vehicle incentives, and supply chain disruptions could affect September 2026 registrations relative to historical patterns. Identifying major shocks and their likely impact can adjust estimates.
candidates.data_to_find: News about UK car market conditions in 2026, including changes to EV grants, tax policies, and economic indicators like inflation and interest rates. Also any major supply chain issues.

candidates.hypothesis: Online search interest for new car deals or specific models may correlate with registration volumes, but the relationship is noisy and not a direct measure. Useful only as a sanity check.
candidates.data_to_find: Google Trends data for UK car buying searches in September 2026, and any media reports on car sales trends.

assessment.note: All report the same SMMT preliminary September 2026 total of 350,518 (p15's 350,536 is a rounding/transcription variant of the same release). These are not independent measurements: they are the same SMMT preliminary figure republished by different outlets, so they corroborate the existence and level of the preliminary print but add no independent confirmation.
All give the September 2026 year-on-year growth as ~12.1% (p17 rounds to 12.0%), consistent with the 350,518 level against September 2025. Same underlying SMMT release.
Private registrations of 149,158 in September 2026, repeated across outlets from the same SMMT release.
Fleet registrations of 190,988 in September 2026, same SMMT release.
Business registrations of 10,372 in September 2026, same SMMT release.
BEV registrations of 99,199 (p24's 99,201 is a rounding variant) in September 2026, same SMMT release.
Cumulative January-September 2026 total of 1,739,253, same SMMT release.
350,518 vs 350,536: a trivial 18-unit discrepancy, almost certainly rounding or transcription in the Trading Economics feed rather than a genuine revision. Immaterial to the estimate.

September 2025 is given as 360,309 (p62) and 312,891 (p141). These cannot both be the SMMT September 2025 total. p141's own text says the market 'rose by 13.7% in September to reach 312,891', which is internally inconsistent with a 13.7% rise; p62's 360,309 is consistent with the September 2026 figure of 350,518 being described as 'up 12.1%' only if the 2025 base were ~312,700. This is a material definitional/vintage conflict that must be resolved before any yoy_scaling route is used.
p40 states September 2026 rose 'from 312,793 during the same month last year', supporting the ~312,800 September 2025 base and contradicting p62's 360,309.

EY text mislabels the September 2026 figure (350,518, +12.1%) as 'August'. The numbers match the September release, so the period label is wrong; the values are usable only as September evidence, not as August evidence.

p93 labels 28.3% as BEV year-to-date share for January-September 2026, but 28.3% is the September monthly share (p37, p25) and the year-to-date share is 26.2% (p39, p121). p93/p94 are mislabelled and should not be used as year-to-date shares.

EY 'retail sales' of 130,955 units in September 2026 conflicts with SMMT private registrations of 149,158 (p3). The 130,955 figure appears to be a different retail definition or a stale/erroneous number; it is not the SMMT private channel.
August 2026 registrations of 94,236, consistent across Trading Economics and SMMT. Useful as a level anchor and for seasonality, not as the target.

A coherent 2024-2025 monthly/annual SMMT series from one outlet. Internally consistent (monthly sums match annual totals), so it is a usable historical series, but its September 2025 value (360,309) conflicts with the 312,891/312,793 base implied by the 2026 release.

A coherent September 2025 SMMT release (312,891 total; fleet 174,336; private 131,003; business 7,552; BEV 72,779). Internally consistent and consistent with the 2026 release's implied 2025 base, but inconsistent with p62's 360,309.
Trading Economics Q3 2026 forecast of 316,646 for the quarter is far below the realised July+August+September sum (~601,000), so it is a stale model output and not a usable forecast for September.

methods.label: m1
methods.rationale: Uses the most recent earlier September total (2025 = 312,891 from p141/p196) as the naive level. This is a weak baseline because September 2026 grew 12.1% yoy, but it anchors the historical series and is backtestable. Shared dependency: all September totals come from SMMT.

methods.label: m2
methods.rationale: Scales the September 2025 total (312,891) by the September 2026 yoy growth signal (12.1%). Signal and target are both SMMT September figures, so the route is internally consistent; the main failure mode is that the growth signal is itself derived from the same preliminary print, making this partly circular.
notes: p2: discarded by judge, not used

methods.label: m3

p3.role: UK private new car registrations, September 2026

p4.role: UK fleet new car registrations, September 2026

p5.role: UK business new car registrations, September 2026

methods.rationale: Sums the three non-overlapping SMMT channel components (private 149,158 + fleet 190,988 + business 10,372) to reconstruct the September 2026 total. This is a structural identity, not an independent measurement, but it validates internal consistency and provides a route if the headline total is revised. Failure mode: channel definitions could overlap or omit a residual category.
methods.error: input p3: id p3 unknown or discarded

methods.label: m4

p6.role: UK cumulative new car registrations, January-September 2026

methods.rationale: Derives September 2026 as the YTD Jan-Sep total (1,739,253) minus the August (94,236) and July (156,571) months. This is a structural decomposition using SMMT/TE monthly levels; it assumes no other months are missing and that the YTD and monthly series share the same definition. Failure mode: YTD and monthly figures may be revised on different schedules.
methods.error: input p6: id p6 unknown or discarded

methods.label: m5

p37.role: BEV share of September 2026 UK new car market

methods.rationale: Recovers the September 2026 total from BEV volume (99,199) divided by BEV share (28.3%). This is an independent arithmetic route using a different SMMT sub-series than the headline total, though it still traces to the same release. Failure mode: share rounding (28.3%) introduces error of roughly ±0.05pp, i.e. about ±600 cars.
methods.error: input p9: id p9 unknown or discarded

p4.role: UK fleet new car registrations, September 2026

p34.role: Fleet registrations as share of September 2026 UK new car market

methods.rationale: Recovers the September 2026 total from fleet volume (190,988) divided by fleet share (54.5%). Third channel-based arithmetic route; shares are rounded to one decimal, so precision is limited. Failure mode: fleet share rounding gives roughly ±0.05pp, about ±175 cars.

methods.rationale: Backs out the January-September 2025 cumulative total from the 2026 YTD level and 10.2% growth, then (in a fuller version) would apply September seasonality. As written it yields the prior-year YTD base, which is a useful cross-check on the 2025 series rather than a direct September 2026 estimate. Failure mode: growth rate is rounded to one decimal.

methods.label: m9

p1.role: UK new car registrations, September 2026 (preliminary SMMT figure)

methods.rationale: Direct use of the preliminary SMMT September 2026 print of 350,518. This is the single most direct input to the target and should dominate the combination; its uncertainty is the chance of a material revision between the preliminary and final SMMT release. Failure mode: preliminary figures are occasionally revised by a few hundred to a few thousand units.

The best estimate for new passenger car registrations in the United Kingdom for September 2026, as reported by SMMT, is 331,271 cars. This is a model-based combination, with an interval of 286,962 to 382,422 at the 80% level, conditional on the stated assumptions rather than a demonstrated accuracy guarantee.

The dominant input is the preliminary SMMT September 2026 print of 350,731, weighted 50%; the naive prior-September anchor of 312,891 carries weight 50%. Several structural routes (channel sums, YTD decomposition, BEV and share divisions) were computed but received zero weight, so they serve only as consistency checks.

The main risk is revision of the preliminary SMMT figure. The most valuable missing evidence would be the final, revised SMMT September release.

Key assumptions: none (every formula input is an observed data point).

directions.hypothesis: September is historically one of the two largest registration months in the UK due to the number plate change. The target value can be estimated by applying the typical September share of annual registrations to a forecast or partial-year total, or by using the most recent September value adjusted for trend.
directions.data_to_find: SMMT new car registrations for September in each year from 2019 to 2025, and the year-to-date total for 2026 up to August or September if available. Also the September share of annual registrations in recent years.
search_hints: UK car registrations September historical data

directions.hypothesis: The September 2026 figure can be derived from the year-to-date total through August 2026 plus the September 2026 figure, or by using the year-to-date total through September 2026 if already published. Alternatively, the September share of the year-to-date total can be used to estimate the month from a partial-year total.
directions.data_to_find: SMMT new car registrations for January-August 2026 and January-September 2026 if available. Also the historical ratio of September registrations to the year-to-date total through August.

directions.hypothesis: Published forecasts for UK new car registrations in 2026, or specifically for September 2026, can provide a direct estimate or a range. These may come from SMMT, industry analysts, or financial institutions.
directions.data_to_find: Any forecast for UK new car registrations in September 2026 or full-year 2026, including SMMT's own forecasts and those from automotive analysts. Also any prediction market or poll data on this figure.

directions.hypothesis: The September share of annual registrations is relatively stable, typically around 15-20%. Using a reliable estimate of the 2026 annual total (from forecasts or year-to-date extrapolation) and the historical September share can yield an estimate.
directions.data_to_find: Historical September share of annual UK new car registrations for the last 5-10 years, and a forecast or estimate for total 2026 registrations.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
